title: Projects & Software

shiftadapt

R package · In development

An R package for adapting and evaluating logistic prediction models under distribution shift.
Implemented updating strategies:

Retain the original model.
Recalibrate the intercept.
Recalibrate the intercept and slope.
Refit the full logistic model.

Intervention selection: Choose the strategy with minimum validation log loss, or use a paired one-standard-error rule to favor a simpler strategy whose validation performance is within one paired standard error of the minimum.
Evaluation: Separate adaptation, validation, and test samples support model fitting, intervention selection, and final performance assessment. Evaluation includes log loss, Brier score, ROC-AUC, and calibration diagnostics.

title: Research
text:
Research Manuscripts


2026 · Unpublished research manuscript


Predictive Stability and Adaptation Under Distribution Shift: Calibration, Discrimination, and Decision Thresholds in Credit-Risk Modeling
Authors: Silas Bambil and Shudeshna Nandy.
A model can continue to rank cases well even when its predicted probabilities become unreliable. This study examines calibration, discrimination, probability accuracy, and decision thresholds using a loan-default benchmark and controlled Monte Carlo experiments.
The experiments consider covariate shift with model misspecification, baseline-risk changes, and changes in predictor effects. Updating strategies include intercept-only recalibration, intercept-and-slope recalibration, importance-weighted refitting, and full deployment refitting. Threshold revision is evaluated separately.
Main finding: The appropriate response depends on how the distribution changes. Intercept recalibration can address baseline-risk changes, while changes in predictor effects may require full refitting. Revising a decision threshold addresses classification decisions rather than probability calibration.
Methods: Logistic regression, Monte Carlo simulation, probability calibration, and evaluation on independent samples.




2026 · Independent research manuscript · Unpublished


Stable Fire-Loss Quantiles and Far-Tail Expected Shortfall Gaps
Author: Silas Bambil.
This study analyzes approximately 1.25 million positive-loss U.S. structure-fire records from NFIRS, covering 2016–2025. Peaks-Over-Threshold methods and Generalized Pareto models are used to estimate extreme loss severity through Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall.
Robustness analyses include threshold sensitivity, parametric bootstrap, annual tail estimation, leave-one-year-out analysis, event-level aggregation, goodness-of-fit diagnostics, and competing tail models.
Main finding: Extreme-loss quantiles were comparatively stable across modeling choices, while Expected Shortfall was more sensitive to threshold selection and uncertainty in the far tail.

Allocating deployment labels
Allocating Deployment Labels Between Model Updating and Intervention Selection Under Distribution Shift
A planned follow-up study asking how a fixed labeling budget should be divided between updating a model and selecting an updating intervention. Planned comparisons include allocating all labels to refitting, fixed fitting–validation splits, cross-fitting, and adaptive allocation, with final evaluation on untouched test data.
